findings.title: Excess shard-aware connection dropped without dec_total_connections()
findings.claim: In the else-if arm for a requested shard, the owned connection is dropped without decrementing total_connections even though it was counted at open, permanently inflating the metric on every shard-aware connection landing on a full bucket; this is an incomplete fix compared to the three other drop sites balanced in commit de164845.

findings.title: Pool teardown on keyspace-channel close leaks the entire total_connections count
findings.claim: When the keyspace-request channel closes and run() returns, PoolRefiller and all its Arc<Connection> entries are dropped with no decrement and no Drop impl, permanently inflating the gauge by the pool's size on every node removal or session drop; the new test drives this path but asserts before it, so it doesn't catch it.

findings.title: Untimed use_keyspace await in start_setting_keyspace_for_connection can wedge the refiller
findings.claim: This await has no timeout (unlike the sibling PoolRefiller::use_keyspace, which wraps its USE in tokio::time::timeout), so a server that accepts the connection but never answers USE leaves the future pending forever, permanently stopping all refills for that node; the PR adds an explicit-failure path but doesn't close this silent-stall path.

findings.title: Sharder/shard-aware-port learning now deferred behind USE success
findings.claim: Hoisting the keyspace check above the sharding block means self.sharder and self.shard_aware_port are no longer updated until USE succeeds, so while USE keeps failing the refiller never learns the node is sharded and keeps dialing the non-shard-aware port; the PR's own test suggests this is intended but the PR description doesn't mention this delay.

findings.title: New tests omit setup_tracing() used by every other test in the module
findings.claim: The two new tests (at :1474 and :1526) don't call setup_tracing() like every other test in the module, so their tracing output is lost on failure.

findings.title: decrement_total_connections loops fetch_sub(1) instead of a single fetch_sub(count)
findings.claim: dec_total_connections() is called in a for loop over count instead of one fetch_sub(count) call; correct but does N atomic RMWs where one would suffice.

findings.title: Pointer logging via {:p} flagged as MEDIUM by pipeline, judged not a real issue
findings.claim: The automated pipeline rated PTREXPOSE-001/002/003 (pointer logging at :683, :981, :1247) as MEDIUM, but the reviewer disagrees, noting these are pre-existing Arc::as_ptr traces at debug/trace level, conventional in this driver and untouched by the PR; the judge's rationale for PTREXPOSE-003 is also factually wrong since the new UseKeyspaceError branch does not call remove_connection.

findings.title: No finding in errors.rs: new ConnectionError variant is semver-safe
findings.claim: ConnectionError is #[non_exhaustive], so the added variant is semver-minor, and #[from] UseKeyspaceError doesn't collide with existing impls — reviewer checked and found no issue.
